questions.question:
Which of the following statements related to MS Word 365 is/are correct?

1) ‘Save’ allows you to update a previously saved file with new content.

2) ‘Save As’ allows you to save a new file or an existing file to a new place with the same name or a different name.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (1) and (2)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Save'** allows you to update a previously saved file with new content. This means any changes made to the document will be stored in the same file without creating a new file.
 
• **'Save As'** allows you to save a new file or an existing file to a new place with the same name or a different name. This is useful when you want to keep the original file unchanged and create a new file with the changes.
 
• **MS Word 365** is a part of the Microsoft Office 365 suite that includes a range of tools for document creation, editing, and collaboration.
 
• Using 'Save' and 'Save As' appropriately can help manage versions of documents and ensure important data is not overwritten unintentionally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Save:**

 
 
• The 'Save' function in MS Word updates the last saved version of the document with the current changes made.
 
• This command is used when you are working on a document and want to ensure that all recent changes are stored in the same file.
 
• The shortcut for 'Save' is Ctrl + S (Windows) or Command + S (Mac).
 
 
 
• **Save As:**
 
 
• The 'Save As' function allows you to save the document in a different location, with a different name, or in a different format.
 
• This is particularly useful when you want to create a copy of the document and retain the original.
 
• It also allows saving the document in formats compatible with other software or older versions of MS Word.
 
• The shortcut for 'Save As' is F12 (Windows) or Shift + Command + S (Mac).

questions.question: What is the function of the ‘Superscript’ feature in Microsoft Word 365?

options.text: Makes the text bold and italic
Adds a line under the text
Makes the text larger and below the baseline
Makes the text smaller and above the baseline

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Makes the text smaller and above the baseline**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The "Superscript" feature in Microsoft Word 365 is a text formatting tool that allows you to raise the selected characters slightly above the baseline of the normal text. 
 
• **Its function and common uses:**
 
 
• Appearance: Superscripted text appears smaller than the surrounding text and is positioned higher, giving it a distinct visual appearance. 
 
• Common Uses:
 
• Mathematical Expressions:
 
• Exponents: For example, "x²" (where the "2" is superscripted to indicate "x squared"). 
 
• Chemical Formulas: Representing chemical compounds with superscripts for charges or isotopes. 
 
• Footnotes and Endnotes:
 
• Displaying small, raised numbers or symbols to indicate references or additional information. 
 
• Ordinal Numbers:
 
• Representing ordinal numbers like "1st," "2nd," "3rd," where the "st," "nd," and "rd" are superscripted. 
 
• Trademarks and Symbols:
 
• Displaying symbols like ® (registered trademark), ™ (trademark), and © (copyright) as superscripts.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement:**
 
 
• Representing units like degrees Celsius (°C) or Fahrenheit (°F) with the degree symbol as a superscript.
 
• How to Use the Superscript Feature in Word 365:
 
• Using the Ribbon:
 
• Select the text you want to format as superscript.
 
• Go to the "Home" tab in the Ribbon.
 
• In the "Font" group, click the "Superscript" button.
 
• Using the Keyboard Shortcut:
 
• Select the text you want to format as superscript.
 
• Press and hold the Ctrl key, Shift key, and the "+" key simultaneously.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the Two - Factor Authentication (2FA)?

options.text: The use of two different credentials to verify identity
A technique for organising files and folders on a PC
A tool for optimising system resources
A security measure to prevent physical damage to a PC

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The use of two different credentials to verify identity**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)** involves the use of two different credentials to verify a user's identity.
 
• These credentials typically include something the user knows (like a password) and something the user has (like a mobile device or hardware token).
 
• 2FA enhances security by adding an additional layer of verification, making it more difficult for unauthorized users to access an account or system.
 
• Common implementations of 2FA include SMS-based codes, authenticator apps, and biometric methods like fingerprint or facial recognition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)** is a subset of multi-factor authentication (MFA), which can involve two or more verification methods.
 
• 2FA is widely used in online banking, email services, and corporate environments to enhance security.
 
• Implementing 2FA can significantly reduce the risk of identity theft, phishing attacks, and other forms of cyber threats.
 
• Some common 2FA methods include Google Authenticator, Authy, and hardware tokens like YubiKey.

questions.question: How do we combine regions from multiple authors into a single Microsoft Word 365 document ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By Combine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Combine" feature in Microsoft Word 365 allows users to merge changes from multiple authors into a single document, making it easier to review and incorporate edits.
 
• This feature is particularly useful for collaborative projects where multiple contributors are working on different parts of a document.
 
• Using "Combine," users can track changes from different authors, ensuring that no contributions are lost or overlooked during the editing process.
 
• The process involves selecting the documents to be combined and then reviewing the changes in the merged document, where each author's edits are highlighted distinctly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combine:**

 
 
• The "Combine" feature is designed for merging multiple versions of a document that have been edited by different authors. It helps in consolidating all changes and comments into one document for easier review and editing.
 
• To use the "Combine" feature, navigate to the "Review" tab in Microsoft Word 365, select "Compare," and then choose "Combine." You can then select the documents you want to merge.
 
• The combined document will show the changes from each author in different colors, making it easy to identify who made which changes.
 
• This feature is essential for maintaining the integrity of collaborative work and ensuring that all contributions are acknowledged and considered.
 
 
 
• **Block Authors:**
 
 
• This feature allows you to restrict certain parts of a document so that only specific authors can edit them. It's useful for protecting sensitive sections of a document from unwanted changes.
 
• To block authors, select the content you want to protect, go to the "Review" tab, and choose "Block Authors."
 
• Blocked sections will have a lock icon, indicating that they are protected from edits by unauthorized users.
 
 
 
• **Restrict Editing:**
 
 
• Restrict Editing is a feature that allows you to control what types of changes can be made to a document. This can include restricting formatting, editing, or allowing only certain types of changes.
 
• To restrict editing, go to the "Review" tab, select "Restrict Editing," and choose the restrictions you want to apply.
 
• This feature is useful for maintaining the structure and formatting of a document while allowing limited editing.
 
 
 
• **Compare:**
 
 
• The "Compare" feature in Microsoft Word 365 allows you to compare two versions of a document and see the differences between them.
 
• To use this feature, go to the "Review" tab, select "Compare," and choose the documents you want to compare.
 
• The comparison will highlight changes, deletions, and additions, making it easy to review the differences between the documents.
 
• This feature is useful for tracking changes over time or comparing contributions from different authors.

questions.question: In a ______ network, all nodes are connected to a single communication line and share it for all their communication needs.

• In a multi-access bus network, **all nodes (computers, printers, etc.) are connected to a single communication line (the bus).**

• Information sent from one node travels along the bus to all other nodes on the network.
 
• It is simple and less expensive to install and expand.
 
• **However, as the number of nodes increases, the efficiency of the network can decrease because of data collisions.**

• There is no signal loss in the Ring Topology.

questions.question: Which of the following is the purpose of the "Zoom" icon in Microsoft Word 365?

options.text: To adjust the visual appearance of our document to suit our reading or editing needs
To change the document's page layout

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**to adjust the visual appearance of our document to suit our reading or editing needs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Zoom icon in Microsoft Word 365 is used to control the magnification level of our document, making it larger or smaller on the screen.
 
• It helps in adjusting the document view to make reading or editing more comfortable depending on our preference.
 
• We can zoom in to get a closer view of the text or zoom out to see more of the page layout at once.
 
• This feature is particularly useful when working with detailed documents or when we have vision difficulties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoom Slider**: Located at the bottom right corner of the Word window, this slider allows us to quickly adjust the zoom level by dragging the slider or clicking the plus (+) or minus (-) buttons.
 
• **Zoom Dialog Box**: We can access more zoom options by clicking on the percentage value next to the zoom slider or by selecting "Zoom" from the "View" tab. This dialog box provides predefined zoom levels, a custom zoom option, and settings to fit the document to the window width, page width, or select multiple pages view.
 
• **Reading Mode**: This feature optimizes the document layout for easier reading, removing unnecessary visual elements and adjusting the zoom level to fit the screen. We can activate it from the "View" tab or the status bar.
 
• **Print Layout vs. Web Layout**: The Zoom feature works in conjunction with different layout views. In Print Layout, we see the document as it would appear when printed, while in Web Layout, the document adapts to fit the screen width, useful for documents intended for online viewing.
 
• **Page Width and Text Width**: Options in the Zoom dialog allow us to fit the document to the width of the page or the width of the text, providing flexibility in how we view our content.

questions.question: Which of the following methods is used to open word Processing package?
Which generation of computers used machine code as the programming language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It is the first generation of computers which uses mechanical language for programming.
 
• The instructions were given through the front panel switches of these computers, directly to the CPU.
 
• The program is written as binary instructions, consisting of zeros and ones.
 
• One of the main disadvantages of programming in a low-level language is that when an error occurs, the code is not as easy to fix.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Machine language, or machine code, is a low-level language comprised of binary digits (ones and zeros). High-level languages, such as Swift and C++ must be compiled into machine language before the code is run on a computer.
 
• Since computers are digital devices, they only recognize binary data. Every program, video, image, and character of text is represented in binary. This binary data, or machine code, is processed as input by the CPU. The resulting output is sent to the operating system or an application, which displays the data visually. For example, the ASCII value for the letter "A" is 01000001 in machine code, but this data is displayed as "A" on the screen. An image may have thousands or even millions of binary values that determine the color of each pixel.
 
• While machine code is comprised of 1s and 0s, different processor architectures use different machine code. For example, a PowerPC processor, which has a RISC architecture, requires different code than an Intel x86 processor, which has a CISC architecture. A compiler must compile high-level source code for the correct processor architecture in order for a program to run correctly.
